provenance.source_to_binary_limit: The immutable load image now has direct PATH/version/SHA256/package ownership and executable-package-manifest verification. Its package version matches the official Ubuntu4.1.0-4build2 source whose timeout-critical semantics were checked. Package verification reports missing documentation/examples/manpage only. This is package/source provenance, not a reproducible rebuild of the executable.

evidence.meaning: Latency histogram allocated with cfg.timeout multiplied by 1000 (microseconds).
Requests/sec calculated from completed response count divided by runtime.
response_complete increments complete and requests before histogram insertion. A rejected insertion increments errors.timeout; the response is already complete and remains in throughput.
Per-connection start timestamp set before sending a new request; elapsed measured at response completion.
Upstream elapsed timing uses gettimeofday; the counter does not identify the physical cause of a large measured elapsed interval.
Default timeout comes from SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS; --timeout can override it.
Histogram limit is maximum plus one; n at or above limit is rejected without updating count, min or max.
Coordinated-omission correction adds in-range histogram samples; it does not restore rejected samples.
Cross-check: same completion and timeout-counter behavior as 4.1.0.

source_verified_meaning.timeout_counter: In reviewed upstream source, the timeout counter counts completed response latencies rejected by the bounded histogram. It is not a counter of requests cancelled by a timer.
source_verified_meaning.throughput: Those completed responses still count in total requests and Requests/sec. HTTP status errors are tracked separately and can overlap with timeout counts.
source_verified_meaning.latency: Reported maximum and percentiles summarize retained, corrected histogram samples. They are not an upper bound over every completed response when timeout is nonzero.
source_verified_meaning.incomplete_requests: This increment occurs only at response completion; unfinished requests left when the run ends do not automatically increment this counter.
source_verified_meaning.counter_64: No special counter cap or automatic end-of-test increment of 64 appears in the reviewed code. Equality with the configured 64 connections does not identify a cause or prove one event per connection.
source_verified_meaning.successful_rps_label: Current controller subtracts only HTTP status errors from raw RPS; completed over-limit responses remain in successful_rps if their HTTP status is successful. Zero-wrk-error ranking remains a separate, existing inclusion condition.
source_verified_meaning.default_boundary_confirmed_for_verified_: The verified Ubuntu ARM64 wrk4.1.0-4build2 source/binary provenance establishes the default histogram ceiling used by this benchmark (no --timeout): elapsed integer microseconds through2000000 inclusive are retained, larger samples increment timeout and are omitted.
source_verified_meaning.default_boundary_conditional_on_installe: Without --timeout, reviewed upstream source accepts elapsed integer microseconds up to 2000000 inclusive; larger values increment timeout and are omitted from histogram statistics. Direct installed-binary identity has now been verified; see provenance artifact.

supported_inference: The displayed maxima below two seconds in these retained examples are compatible with positive timeout counters because over-limit completed samples are excluded from the histogram. This is a statement about accounting, not a diagnosis of the elapsed-time cause.
unresolved_limits: No per-request route, status, timestamp, connection identity or rejected-latency values are retained for these counters.
These aggregate records cannot distinguish service delay, client scheduling, host/VM behavior, network behavior or clock behavior. No cause is assigned.
No evidence here establishes a harness fault or authorizes a change to the fixed ranking rule.
changes: Only this new diagnostic JSON was written. Measurement records, classifiers, application source, controller and shared fixtures were left unchanged.

downstream_source_review.integrity_limit: Both source tar archives match SHA256 and byte sizes listed by the .dsc fetched over HTTPS from the official Ubuntu archive. The .dsc OpenPGP signature was not independently validated in this review.

build_rules.content:
#!/usr/bin/make -f

include /usr/share/dpkg/architecture.mk
include /usr/share/dpkg/pkg-info.mk

BINDIR=$(CURDIR)/debian/wrk/usr/bin

ifneq (,$(filter $(DEB_HOST_ARCH), armel mips mipsel powerpc))
	LIBS += -latomic
	export LIBS
endif

export DEB_BUILD_MAINT_OPTIONS = hardening=+all

%:
	dh $@

override_dh_auto_build:
	dh_auto_build -- WITH_LUAJIT=/usr WITH_OPENSSL=/usr VER=debian/$(DEB_VERSION)

override_dh_installman:
	help2man --no-info --name="a modern HTTP benchmarking tool" --version-string=$(DEB_VERSION_UPSTREAM) $(BINDIR)/wrk > debian/wrk.1
	dh_installman

critical_findings: Official Ubuntu orig src/wrk.c, src/wrk.h and src/stats.c are byte-identical to upstream tag 4.1.0.
The single downstream patch does not change src/wrk.c or src/wrk.h: response-completion accounting, default 2000ms timeout, histogram allocation, elapsed timing and RPS formula are unchanged.

The stats.c patch replaces legacy atomic operations with sequentially consistent __atomic operations for histogram counts and min/max updates. The rejection condition n >= stats->limit and zero return remain unchanged; successful in-range insertion still returns one.
Other patch changes concern Makefile system libraries/build flags and a Lua API type alias in src/script.c; neither changes timeout accounting.
debian/rules uses system LuaJIT/OpenSSL, hardening flags and a Debian package version string. No timeout/default-limit or completion-accounting override appears in the inspected package rules.
downstream_source_review.conclusion: The inspected Ubuntu 4.1.0-4build2 source package preserves the previously described timeout-counter semantics and default two-second histogram ceiling. This source check still does not prove which installed executable PATH resolves to in the benchmark image.
downstream_source_review.resource_scope: Small HTTPS downloads (about 69KB compressed package metadata/source plus three upstream text files); archives inspected in memory. No extraction into application trees, builds, containers or workloads.
